analysis.title: Signal over Noise: The looming agentic disruption
key_insights: UBS CIO argues the internet is shifting from human browsing to autonomous AI agents acting between users and the digital world. When the main visitor is software, digital advertising and enterprise SaaS are disrupted.
Digital advertising: agents executing purchases lead to zero-click commerce. Agents do not respond to emotional ads or retargeting banners, so value moves from human attention to an agentic outcome.

Brands must shift from B2C to B2A (business to agent). Traditional SEO is no longer enough, and brands need to optimize for agentic discovery by exposing machine-readable product data and real-time inventory.
Enterprise software: per-seat SaaS pricing assumes headcount growth. One AI-augmented employee or autonomous workflow can do the work of five to 10 people, so enterprises need fewer seats.
Agents can interact directly with underlying databases via protocols, so they do not need a graphical interface. This could make the traditional SaaS dashboard obsolete.

The unifying threat across advertising and software is intermediation. The interface moves upstream to the agent, and companies that serve machines first and humans second will likely define the next decade of tech.

Adoption data on personal agents: OpenClaw gained 100,000 GitHub stars in its first eight days, Muse reached 10 million US downloads in 40 days, and Instinct reported 40% of users connected credit cards to its agentic assistant by week three.

UBS believes the market still underappreciates the speed of AI disruption. Its advice is to stay diversified beyond megacap index concentration, since concentration trades on who leads today while diversification invests in who could lead tomorrow.

sector_views.rationale: Agents in zero-click commerce do not respond to attention-based advertising, so value shifts from human attention to agentic outcomes. The report does not state a formal rating.
Per-seat pricing and graphical interfaces are challenged when agents do the work of 5-10 people and can access databases directly. The report does not state a formal rating.
